visualReview.notes: Inspected current portable exterior views. The two surviving sandstone ranges, penitentiary dormitory, enclosure wall and three-part Girls Home are legible. A revised roof joins the timber covered way end to end. Chimney bases intersect their roof slopes.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected nine contextual shared-surface captures and confirmed unload. Sandstone, darker brick, tile, weatherboard and pale window trim remain distinct. The school’s sandstone center and Victorian wings read separately.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 25 contextual frames, including all four detail levels and their transitions. Both institutional groups and the masonry enclosure retain their footprint and silhouettes. Street and closeup resolve chimneys, dormers, sash, braces and coping.

geographicReview.notes: The two precincts were matched to the numbered NSW conservation plan and the open mapped footprints. The original 384 m terrain raster and terrain-mounted capture were inspected. The penitentiary envelope was registered using the two mapped sandstone ranges, with a 2.91 m cross-check against the nearby Ward 1 center. Ground and floor elevations remain approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Standing heritage exteriors of the Parramatta Female Factory and adjacent former Roman Catholic Orphan School and Parramatta Girls Home, including the two original sandstone ranges, penitentiary dormitory, solitary-cell enclosure wall, the school’s main building and its covered way and southwest range.
fidelityReview.notes: The model represents the principal standing heritage exteriors on each side of the enclosure. The recorded sandstone and brick masses, roof types and the school’s covered timber way carry the identifiable forms. Dormitory registration, exact roof pitches, opening placements, later additions and footings are approximate.

imageryReview.notes: The published Qualla Augustus Earle watercolour matched the native Wikimedia original byte for byte. The National Library of Australia identifies it as the same circa 1826 object. It provides historical context for the penitentiary wing and factory ranges. The documented later fabric uses mapped geometry and written conservation descriptions.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Principal standing Parramatta Female Factory and former Girls Home heritage exteriors, with the Solitary Cell Block enclosure and the school’s timber covered way.

limitations: The model represents the standing central heritage exteriors and the connecting school range. It depicts the original prison site and the later orphan school and Girls Home in their surviving form.

The southwest range footprint also includes adjoining courtyard fabric. Roof pitches, bay divisions, later additions and surface detailing are estimates derived from the written descriptions and plan geometry.

The principal dormitory footprint was registered from the official conservation plan using mapped neighbors. Fixture locations, façade openings, wall footings and foundation elevations remain approximate.
The independent ground samples are unchanged. They capture the river terrace broadly and do not provide surveyed floor levels.
